title: READY FOR MS: Development, piloting and validation of an online program to promote resilience in multiple sclerosis
summary:
People with multiple sclerosis (MS) suffer not only from physical symptoms—psychological stressors such as fatigue, concentration problems, depression, and anxiety also have a significant impact on their daily lives. Coping with the disease, its unpredictable course, and the challenges of everyday life requires a high degree of inner strength—known as resilience.
This is exactly where the READY for MS program comes in. It is based on Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)—a modern form of behavioral therapy that focuses on mindfulness, acceptance, and personal values. The aim is to strengthen psychological flexibility—the ability to remain capable of acting and balanced even in difficult times.
READY for MS was developed as an online intervention and consists of seven modules and an additional refresher unit. It is specifically aimed at people with MS and promotes five key factors for greater resilience: positive emotions, flexible thinking (e.g., acceptance), meaning and orientation in life, social support, and active coping strategies.
The program combines proven behavioral therapy techniques—such as mindfulness, relaxation, and values work—with practical exercises for everyday life. Initial studies show that READY can help reduce stress and significantly improve quality of life.
Our goal: to make READY for MS available as an online service in Germany—for greater self-efficacy, quality of life, and mental strength in dealing with MS.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants must have a confirmed diagnosis of MS (verified by a doctor's letter no more than one year old). In addition, participants must be able to read and understand German texts and have a smartphone, tablet, or computer with internet access.
Exclusion criteria:
Only severe mental impairments (e.g. severe depression, dementia) are defined as exclusion criteria.
